text:
support-bot: Alert: observed p99 latency increase (~2.3x) for model redwood-llama-13b in eu-west-1 since 2024-11-02 09:12 UTC. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/latency?cohort=eu-west
maria: seeing same in internal canary dashboards, p95 up ~1.4x, p99 tail looks shifted
ajay: which rollout triggered? runtime version v2024.11.02-b3 went to 10% at 09:00
kim: I think that runtime had the new kernel-selector change + quant-scheduler bump
sara: customer escalation: ACME corp reporting 2.2s p99 for chat endpoints (was ~900ms)
ajay: canary telemetry shows KV cache cold starts spike around 09:07 for some hosts
maria: reproable w/ synthetic load? anyone have a curl we can use
ajay: use this short repro:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-13b","prompt":"hello"}'
```
maria: thanks, I'll run against the canary pool
deploy-bot: rolled v2024.11.02-b3 -> cohort=canary(10%) at 09:00 by ajay
kim: hypothesis: kernel-selector changed batch assignment -> more late binding + smaller batches -> higher p99 overhead
sara: trying traffic split rollback: can we pin canary hosts back to v2024.11.01? ajay pls
ajay: starting rollback for cohort, routing 10% -> old runtime for affected tenant groups now
maria: collecting perf traces: enabling pprof and perf on 3 sample hosts, dumping KV cache metrics, collecting /proc/sched
maria: attaching quick sample: host-12 kvcache-misses increased 4x, batch-size median dropped from 16 -> 6
kim: sounds like the scheduler change pushed smaller batches, which increases per-token overhead and tail latency
sara: mitigation: increase batching window on canary pool to 25ms and revert kernel-selector config
ajay: applied batching-window=25ms on canary at 09:45
support-bot: alert auto-updated: p99 decreased from 2.3s -> 1.1s in 15m for canary
maria: still seeing customer p99 for ACME at 1.2s, but trending down. running longer soak
sara: next steps: keep canary pinned until we finish bisect test; recreate small sandbox with kernel-selector=off and run synthetic cohort
kim: I'll run a perf+trace bisect between kernel-selector commit c1a2f and quant-scheduler commit d3b4e
ajay: note: if rollback reduces cost predictably, we'll roll forward with adjusted kernel-selector heuristics
maria: I've filed follow-up bug: #INF-1248 with logs + perf traces
sara: marking owners: ajay (rollback/rollforward), maria (traces/soak), kim (bisect)
ajay: will update in 30 min with rollback status
maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
